thread:
incident-bot: PAGING on-call: latency SLO breach for customer NovaPay (single-tenant). p95 1.2s -> 2.1s, p99 0.82s -> 2.8s, streaming stalls observed. Please ack and triage.

alex.chen: acked. jumping in. @oncall-night please standby for handoff in ~10m if this persists.

priya.nair: adding context from alerts: spike started ~08:04 UTC, correlates with a burst of requests from nova-tenant-v2 (ip range 10.32.0.0/16). concurrency max spiked to 420, avg request size up ~3x.

jonas-w: I see repeated backpressure logs in the runtime: `request_queue_time` jumped and many streams hung waiting on flush. linking logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/prod/streams/177200

maria.gomez: pinging product / account — NovaPay reports timeouts in their payment flows, they flagged 08:10 UTC. Impacting checkout webhooks for ~5% of requests (retries observed).

alex.chen: hypothesis: streaming stalls due to many short-lived concurrent streams + SSE proxy backlog. two-pronged mitigation: 1) route NovaPay to a lower-latency fallback model variant (same family, smaller kv/quant profile) 2) throttle tenant concurrency via runtime policy.

jonas-w: quick checks:
```
# check runtime queue lengths
kubectl -n runtime exec -it runtime-proxy-0 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep request_queue_time"
# tail decode latencies
grep -i "decode_time" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log | tail -n 50
```

priya.nair: grabbing traces from tracing service for two sample requests that hit p99. looks like 60% of time spent in `token_decode` for those requests, token lengths ~1200 vs usual 80. unusual prompt construction (JSON blob + repeated system messages).

eng-runtime-bot: observed model variant `redwood-beta-13b-quant` had a decode spike at high concurrency due to cache eviction pattern. fallback `redwood-beta-13b-q8n-lite` has faster decode for mid-length sequences.

oncall-night: I'm on shift now, can take lead. starting mitigation steps.

alex.chen: plan of action (live):
- route nova-tenant-v2 -> fallback model variant via routing policy (canary immediate)
- set `tenant.max_concurrency=60` for nova-tenant-v2 for 30 min
- temporarily disable streaming (SSE) for this tenant to avoid proxy stalls, serve full payloads instead
- scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes (hot patch)
- continue tracing p99/p95 and surface to customer

jonas-w: executing route change now: `POST /admin/routing` payload -> `{tenant: "nova-tenant-v2", model: "redwood-beta-13b-q8n-lite", weight: 1.0}` 

support-bot: notifying customer via escalation channel: "NovaPay engineering — we're actively mitigating a tail-latency issue and will update in 15m. Current mitigation: transient routing + concurrency limit."

priya.nair: applying tenant concurrency cap: `redwood-cli tenants update nova-tenant-v2 --set max_concurrency=60 --ttl 30m`

eng-runtime-bot: scaling pool: `./infra/scale_pool --pool dedicated-nova --delta 2` -> nodes provisioning started (estimated 90s).

(5 minutes pass)

alex.chen: Observability update: after routing to q8n-lite + concurrency cap + disabling streaming: p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 540ms, p99 from 2.8s -> 720ms. Some residual stalls but much improved.

maria.gomez: passing update to NovaPay: "We've applied transient routing to a faster model variant and limited peak concurrency. Latency p99 improved from ~2.8s -> ~0.72s. We're keeping this in place while we investigate root cause."

jonas-w: digging into cause: combination of factors:
- unusually large prompt templates that include repeated system instructions and nested JSON arrays -> higher tokenization + decode overhead
- tenant had many small parallel chat sessions with streaming enabled, causing many tiny batches and SSE proxy backpressure
- `redwood-beta-13b-quant` kernel path had a degenerative kernel choice for sequences ~500-1500 tokens under heavy MLP contention, leading to cache thrashing and decode slowdowns.

priya.nair: added checklist for permanent mitigations:
- provide NovaPay guidance: canonicalize prompts (remove repeated system blocks), enforce max prompt length via gateway rules
- add tenant-level streaming backpressure control (auto-fallback to non-streaming when queue_time > threshold)
- patch runtime kernel selector to avoid degenerative path for mid-length sequences under high concurrency (ENG-RUNTIME ticket created)
- consider warm-up cache for single-tenant heavy users during traffic spikes

alex.chen: immediate post-incident actions:
- we're keeping routing & concurrency cap for 30m, then will gradually roll back if stable
- open incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime (jonas) + eng-ml (priya) for root cause
- scheduled customer sync in 1h to review impact and ask for example prompts

jonas-w: created ENGINC-2026: runtime-kernel-degen, assigned to @eng-runtime with priority P1, includes reproducer, perf traces, and failing log excerpts.

oncall-night: handing off to morning oncall at 12:00 UTC — will attach runbook and current mitigations.

support-bot: posting timeline to NovaPay slack and creating support ticket `SUP-9931`, includes mitigation summary and request for representative prompt examples.

(45 minutes later)

alex.chen: rolling back scale: pool scaled back to baseline. leaving routing & concurrency cap in place for now; will remove routing in a controlled canary if p99 stays < 0.9s for 30m.

maria.gomez: customer update: NovaPay confirmed retries dropped and checkout failure rate back to baseline, asked for the root cause analysis and follow-up.

jonas-w: root-cause summary to include: spike due to mixed workload patterns (long prompts + high concurrency streaming), degenerative kernel path under specific token-length band, and proxy backpressure. mitigation: tenant-level concurrency caps, streaming auto-fallback, kernel selector patch, prompt guidance.

alex.chen: thanks team. saving logs/traces to ENGINC-2026, will draft postmortem. closing thread when morning oncall confirms stability. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime-bot: incident-bot: incident marked as "mitigated" at 1772006732.
